pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist — the whole countryside crowded into the wood to hear one man preach, for the choirmaster a Psalm of the sons of Korah, hear this all you peoples
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_sermon_of_saint_john_the_baptist

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Tower of Babel — the tower of all the nations rising in its tiers over the harbor and the town, listen all inhabitants of the world, both low and high
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_tower_of_babel

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Apostle Paul — the old apostle at his table with the pen in his hand and the open book in front of him, rich and poor alike, my mouth will impart wisdom
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_apostle_paul

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Netherlandish Proverbs — a village where every proverb of the people is being acted out at once, and the meditation of my heart will bring understanding, I will incline my ear to a proverb
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_netherlandish_proverbs

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Saul and David — David with his hands on the strings of the harp playing before the troubled king, I will express my riddle with the harp, why should I fear in times of trouble
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_saul_and_david

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Taking of Christ — the armed men closing in around Christ in the dark and laying their hands on Him, when wicked usurpers surround me, they trust in their wealth
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_taking_of_christ

pictures.scene: Marinus van Reymerswaele, A Moneychanger and His Wife — the pair bent over the scales and the coins with the ledger open between them, and boast in their great riches, no man can possibly redeem his brother
pictures.name: pd_van_reymerswaele_a_moneychanger_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Carrying the Cross — Christ holding the beam of the cross with both hands and His eyes lifted, or pay his ransom to God, for the redemption of his soul is costly
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_christ_carrying_the_cross

pictures.scene: Pieter Claesz, Vanitas Still Life — the skull and the bones laid on the table beside the overturned glass and the painter's own palette, and never can payment suffice, that he should live on forever
pictures.name: pd_claesz_vanitas_still_life

pictures.scene: Frans Hals, Young Man with a Skull — the young man in the plumed hat holding a skull out toward the viewer, and not see decay, for it is clear that wise men die
pictures.name: pd_hals_young_man_with_a_skull

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Parable of the Rich Fool — the old man counting his gold by candlelight among the money bags on the night his soul is required of him, and the foolish and the senseless both perish, and leave their wealth to others
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_parable_of_the_rich_fool

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Abbey in the Oakwood — the gravestones standing in the snow among the dead oaks before the broken abbey, their graves are their eternal homes, their dwellings for endless generations
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_abbey_in_the_oakwood

pictures.scene: Hubert Robert, A Hermit Praying in the Ruins of a Roman Temple — one old man kneeling in the ruin of a building raised to somebody's name, even though their lands were their namesakes, but a man despite his wealth cannot endure
pictures.name: pd_robert_a_hermit_praying_in_the_ruins_of_a_roman_temple

pictures.scene: Frans Snyders, Still Life with Dead Game — the boar's head laid out among the kill on the table of the hunt, he is like the beasts that perish, this is the fate of the foolish
pictures.name: pd_snyders_still_life_with_dead_game

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Parable of the Blind — each man holding the stick of the man in front of him as the leader goes down into the ditch, and their followers who endorse their sayings, Selah
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_the_parable_of_the_blind

pictures.scene: Jean-François Millet, The Sheepfold Moonlight — the flock driven into the fold under the moon with the shepherd shutting the hurdle behind them, like sheep they are destined for Sheol, death will be their shepherd
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_sheepfold_moonlight

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, Morning in the Riesengebirge — the first light coming over range after range of mountains with the crucifix standing on the summit rock, the upright will rule them in the morning, and their form will decay in Sheol
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_morning_in_the_riesengebirge

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Noli Me Tangere — the risen Christ standing in the garden before the opened tomb while Mary kneels and reaches out to Him, far from their lofty abode, but God will redeem my life from Sheol
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_noli_me_tangere

pictures.scene: Giuseppe Angeli, Elijah Taken Up in a Chariot of Fire — the prophet carried up out of the world in the flames with the wheel of the chariot beside him, for He will surely take me to Himself, Selah
pictures.name: pd_angeli_elijah_taken_up_in_a_chariot_of_fire

pictures.scene: Jacob van Ruisdael, Bentheim Castle — the great house standing on the height above the woods and the little roofs of the village below it, do not be afraid when a man grows rich, when the splendor of his house increases
pictures.name: pd_ruisdael_bentheim_castle

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, Death and the Miser — the man in green still reaching into the money chest while the demons wait under it and the armor lies abandoned on the floor, for when he dies he will carry nothing away, his abundance will not follow him down
pictures.name: pd_bosch_death_and_the_miser

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Prodigal Son in the Tavern — the young man laughing with the tall glass raised over his head while the feast is still going, though in his lifetime he blesses his soul, and men praise you when you prosper
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_the_prodigal_son_in_the_tavern

pictures.scene: Gustave Courbet, A Burial at Ornans — the whole village standing round the open grave behind the crucifix and the priest, he will join the generation of his fathers, who will never see the light of day
pictures.name: pd_courbet_a_burial_at_ornans

pictures.scene: Rosa Bonheur, Ploughing in the Nivernais — the yoked oxen hauling the plough through the broken ground with the driver walking at their heads, a man who has riches without understanding is like the beasts that perish
pictures.name: pd_bonheur_ploughing_in_the_nivernais

lines.text: For the choirmaster. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.
Hear this, all you peoples;
listen, all inhabitants of the world,
both low and high,
rich and poor alike.
My mouth will impart wisdom,
and the meditation of my heart will bring understanding.
I will incline my ear to a proverb;
I will express my riddle with the harp:
Why should I fear in times of trouble,
when wicked usurpers surround me?
They trust in their wealth
and boast in their great riches.
No man can possibly redeem his brother
or pay his ransom to God.
For the redemption of his soul is costly,
and never can payment suffice,
that he should live on forever
and not see decay.
For it is clear that wise men die,
and the foolish and the senseless both perish
and leave their wealth to others.
Their graves are their eternal homes—
their dwellings for endless generations—
even though their lands were their namesakes.
But a man, despite his wealth, cannot endure;
he is like the beasts that perish.
This is the fate of the foolish
and their followers who endorse their sayings.
Selah
Like sheep they are destined for Sheol.
Death will be their shepherd.
The upright will rule them in the morning,
and their form will decay in Sheol,
far from their lofty abode.
But God will redeem my life from Sheol,
for He will surely take me to Himself.
Selah
Do not be afraid when a man grows rich,
when the splendor of his house increases.
For when he dies, he will carry nothing away;
his abundance will not follow him down.
Though in his lifetime he blesses his soul—
and men praise you when you prosper—
he will join the generation of his fathers,
who will never see the light of day.
A man who has riches without understanding
is like the beasts that perish.
